title: Putting the patient journey first
html:
Reflecting on Rock Dental’s triumph at the 2025 Private Dentistry Awards, Anoup Nandra and Simran Bains reveal the key to a successful referral dental practice.

Winning Patient Care Midlands and Referral Practice North at the Private Dentistry Awards 2025 was an incredibly proud moment for the whole team at Rock Dental.

While the awards themselves were a wonderful recognition, for us they represented something much bigger: an acknowledgement of the way our team has worked to build a referral service where clinical expertise and patient experience are given equal importance.

A referral can be a relatively small part of a clinician’s working day, but for the patient being referred, it can feel significant. They may be attending an unfamiliar practice, meeting a new clinician and facing treatment they already perceive to be complex. There may be anxiety around what will happen, why they have been referred and what their treatment journey will involve.

At Rock Dental, we believe excellent referral care starts by recognising this.

A continuation of care

One of our priorities is ensuring patients never feel as though they have been ‘passed on’. From the moment a referral arrives, our aim is to create a clear and reassuring journey for both the patient and referring clinician.

Our referral team plays an integral role in this. Communication, organisation and accessibility are as important to the overall experience as what happens once the patient enters the surgery.

Patients need to understand why they are attending, what their appointment will involve and what the next steps may look like.

That communication continues following assessment and treatment. We value the trust placed in us by our referring colleagues and respect the relationship they have established with their patients.

Where someone has been referred for a specific aspect of treatment, our role is to complement the care already being provided, communicate clearly throughout and return the patient to their dentist with confidence.

It is this mutual trust that has allowed us to build long-standing relationships with clinicians who refer their patients to Rock Dental.

The strength of multidisciplinary care

One of the greatest strengths of a referral practice is the ability to bring different areas of dentistry together.

At Rock Dental, our team provides care across oral surgery, implant dentistry, periodontics, endodontics and complex restorative dentistry, alongside orthodontic, cosmetic and general dental care. For patients whose needs cross several disciplines, this creates an opportunity for genuine collaboration.

Rather than viewing a tooth, implant or periodontal problem in isolation, we consider the wider picture and how each stage of treatment may affect the next. Clinicians can discuss cases together, review imaging and records and consider the patient’s overall oral health and long-term outcome.

Our regular multidisciplinary discussions are particularly valuable when planning more complex cases. By bringing together clinicians from different disciplines, we can carefully consider the most appropriate treatment plan for each individual patient, including the sequence and timing of each stage, which clinicians should be involved and at what point in the journey.

This collaborative approach allows every aspect of treatment to be thoughtfully planned, with each stage complementing the next and the team working towards a shared clinical goal.

It also gives patients greater continuity. Rather than navigating multiple practices and separate treatment plans, their care can be coordinated within one familiar environment, supported by a team who understands their wider treatment journey.

Patient care is a team responsibility

Exceptional patient care cannot be delivered by clinicians alone.

A patient’s experience begins long before they enter the surgery. It starts with their first telephone call, the way their questions are answered, the efficiency with which their referral is managed and the welcome they receive when they walk through our doors.

Our reception team, referral coordinators, treatment coordinators and dental nurses are therefore integral to our patient-care model.

‘With growth comes a responsibility to ensure the personal experience patients value is never lost’

As Rock Dental has grown, we have developed defined roles within the team to ensure patients receive the right support at every stage, while maintaining consistent communication. Our nursing team also works across different areas of dentistry, giving them a broader understanding of how different disciplines connect. This is particularly valuable when supporting patients through several stages of treatment.

Behind the scenes, there can be considerable coordination involved in making a complex treatment journey feel straightforward. Every interaction contributes to how supported and cared for a patient feels.

Caring for anxious or nervous patients

Every patient arrives with a different history, different expectations and a different relationship with dentistry. Understanding this is fundamental to the way we provide care.

For some patients, walking into a dental practice can itself be a significant step. They may have avoided treatment because of anxiety or previous negative experiences, and being referred for more complex treatment can understandably heighten those concerns.

For these patients, clinical expertise must be accompanied by empathy. This may mean allowing additional time, explaining each stage before it happens, agreeing a signal to pause treatment or giving the patient an opportunity to tell us what they are worried about.

Where appropriate, sedation can form part of this pathway, but managing dental anxiety extends far beyond sedation. The environment, language we use, continuity of care and giving patients a sense of control can all fundamentally change their experience. This becomes particularly important when care involves several disciplines or multiple stages of treatment. What is familiar to us as clinicians can understandably feel overwhelming to a patient.

For more complex multidisciplinary cases, we provide detailed treatment plan letters setting out the proposed journey, including the stages of treatment and clinicians involved.

This allows patients to take the information away, digest it in their own time and discuss it with those close to them if they wish. We also offer time to discuss their treatment plan further and answer questions before any decisions are made. We want patients to feel informed, comfortable and confident about the care they choose.

Clear communication creates confidence

Patients should understand the care they are receiving and feel confident in the decisions they make.

We place considerable importance on explaining diagnoses and treatment options clearly and in a way that is appropriate for the individual. Complex dentistry can involve a great deal of information, so we support conversations with written information where appropriate, particularly for treatments such as root canal therapy, periodontal treatment and implant dentistry.

Patients can also meet with our treatment coordinator to discuss questions about their journey. We want them to have the opportunity to consider their options and understand the benefits, limitations and alternatives before proceeding.

‘Clinical excellence is naturally at the heart of a referral practice, but exceptional care extends far beyond the treatment itself’

Consent, in our view, is an ongoing conversation. Communication with referring clinicians is equally important.

Clear correspondence following consultations and treatment maintains continuity and ensures everyone involved understands what has been completed, any recommendations made and what should happen next.

Growing without losing the personal approach

Rock Dental has changed considerably over the years, growing from a small practice into a purpose-built, five-surgery multidisciplinary practice with a team of around 30. With growth comes a responsibility to ensure the personal experience patients value is never lost.

We have worked hard to introduce systems and defined responsibilities without allowing those systems to replace human interaction.

Regular team meetings, huddles and multidisciplinary discussions allow us to share ideas, discuss challenges and learn from one another. Patient feedback is equally valuable, giving us an opportunity to view the practice through the patient’s eyes and continually refine the experience we provide.

Education and shared learning are also an important part of our referral culture. In collaboration with the College of General Dentistry (CGDent), we host study clubs at Rock Dental where clinicians from surrounding practices can bring cases to discuss directly with members of our referral team.

This may be a case they would like to treat themselves but where they value another clinical perspective, or a case they are considering referring. In the latter situation, they have the opportunity to discuss it directly with, and meet, the clinician who may go on to care for their patient. These evenings create an open environment for shared learning while strengthening relationships between our referral team and local clinicians.

Supporting referring colleagues is, for us, an extension of supporting their patients; whether that results in a referral or gives the clinician greater confidence to manage the case within their own practice.

More than the treatment provided

Winning Patient Care and Referral Practice in the same year was particularly meaningful because, to us, the two are inseparable.

Clinical excellence is naturally at the heart of a referral practice, but exceptional care extends far beyond the treatment itself.

It is the combination of clinical expertise, thoughtful planning, clear communication and a genuinely personal approach that shapes the patient’s experience. Every element should work together to ensure each patient feels understood, supported and confident in their care.

‘The Private Dentistry Awards were an incredibly special recognition for Rock Dental, but they also gave us an opportunity to reflect on what patient care means to us’

Patients may not remember every clinical detail of their treatment, but they will remember whether they felt listened to, whether somebody took the time to explain their options and whether they felt genuinely cared for.

When a colleague refers a patient to us, they are placing trust in our entire team. Protecting that trust means providing the level of care we would want for our own patients while respecting the relationship they have already established.

The Private Dentistry Awards were an incredibly special recognition for Rock Dental, but they also gave us an opportunity to reflect on what patient care means to us. It isn’t one initiative, protocol or person; it is a culture created through the decisions and interactions that take place across the practice every day.

At Rock Dental, we value the relationship between our team, the patient and the referring clinician. By communicating openly, planning carefully and working collaboratively throughout the patient’s journey, we can provide care that feels considered, coordinated and personal from beginning to end.
